> If smooth_idf=True (the default), the constant “1” is added to the numerator and denominator of the idf as if an extra document was seen containing every term in the collection exactly once, which prevents zero divisions: idf(t) = log [ (1 + n) / (1 + df(t)) ] + 1.

title: Using pretrained models in step_tokenize_sentencepiece
description:
I'm trying to use bpe working in step_tokenize_sentencepiece.

Could I use some already trained model? Here some examples trying different approaches:

```
library(tidymodels)
library(textrecipes)
library(sentencepiece)

dataf <- data.frame(
  "text" = c("positive sentiment", "super neg", "bad outcome", "good results"),
  "label_col" = c("pos", "neg", "neg", "pos", "neg")
)

test <- data.frame(
  "text" = c("negative results", "neg"),
  "label_col" = c("neg", "neg")
)

rec0 <- dataf |> 
  recipe(label_col ~ text) |> 
  step_tokenize_sentencepiece(text, vocabulary_size = 25) |> 
  step_tfidf(text) 

# It splits by character not by "bpe"
rec0 |> 
  prep() |> 
  juice() |>
  print()


# 0.853 for .pred_neg in the first case
rec0 |> 
  workflow(logistic_reg()) |> 
  fit(dataf) |> 
  augment(test, type = c("prob", "class"))

# I can't split by bpe in step_tokenize_sentencepiece
tryCatch({
    rec1 <- dataf |> 
      recipe(label_col ~ text) |> 
      step_tokenize_sentencepiece(text, vocabulary_size = 25, options = list(type = "bpe")) |> 
      step_tfidf(text) 

    rec1 |> 
      prep() |> 
      juice() |>
      print()
  },
  error = \(e) message(e)
)

# I can do it in step_tokenize_bpe
rec2 <- dataf |> 
  recipe(label_col ~ text) |> 
  step_tokenize_bpe(text) |>   
  step_tfidf(text) 

rec2 |> 
  prep() |> 
  juice() |>
  print()

# 1.00 for .pred_neg in the first case
rec2 |> 
  workflow(logistic_reg()) |> 
  fit(dataf) |> 
  augment(test, type = c("prob", "class"))


# Using a sentencepiece trained model before
all <- bind_rows(dataf |> mutate(data = "train"), test |> mutate(data = "test"))
download.file("https://bpemb.h-its.org/en/en.wiki.bpe.vs1000.model", "en.wiki.bpe.vs1000.model")
model <- sentencepiece_load_model("en.wiki.bpe.vs1000.model")
all$text <- sentencepiece_encode(model, all$text, type = "subwords") |> 
  tokenlist()

rec3 <- all |> 
  filter(data == "train") |>
  recipe(label_col ~ text) |> 
  step_tfidf(text) 

rec3 |> 
  prep() |> 
  juice() |>
  print()

rec3 |> 
  workflow(logistic_reg()) |> 
  fit(all |> filter(data == "train")) |> 
  augment(all |> filter(data == "test"), type = c("prob", "class"))



# Using a sentencepiece trained model before
# Using word embedings instead of step_tfidf

download.file("https://bpemb.h-its.org/en/en.wiki.bpe.vs1000.model", "en.wiki.bpe.vs1000.model")
```

title: step_pos_filter() should have a remove_tags argument
Step order help messages
description:
Once https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/issues/147 is finished, it is going to be easier to write messages to the user related to the use steps. We don't generally do this for recipe steps, but the steps in {textrecipes} are more interconnected than most recipe steps so we will make an exception.

Say you have the following recipe

```r
recipe(outcome ~ text, data = data) %>%
  step_bpe_tokenize(text, n_tokenns = 1000) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(text, max_tokens = 500)
```

This would most likely be nonsensical since the vocabulary size is defined in `step_bpe_tokenize()`. Having `step_tokenfilter()` throw a message to the user would be helpful here. Similarly `step_tokenize() %>% step_tfidf()` could have an message telling the user to filter the tokens before creating columns.

I would like these just to be messages with a global option `textrecipes.tips` to turn all of these off as there are times where the tips will be wrong.

title: Duplicated dense/sparse weighting logic in tf_weight()/tf_weight_sparse() is a drift risk
description:
## Problem

Each weighting scheme in R/tf.R is implemented twice (`tf_weight` for dense, `tf_weight_sparse` for sparse). A recent audit's cross-check of the two paths is exactly what surfaced the "double normalization" NaN gap (#325) — present only in the dense path, and entirely absent (not even a case) in the sparse path. Two independent implementations of the same math will keep drifting.

## Suggested change

Consider unifying to a single implementation parameterized by sparsity, or add a standing test that asserts dense/sparse identity for every scheme on the same fixture, run in CI.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **B7**.

title: Add value-level (not just shape-level) tests for weighting/feature-extraction steps
description:
## Problem

`test-tf.R`, `test-tfidf.R`, `test-textfeature.R`, `test-lda.R`, `test-ngram.R`, `test-texthash.R`, and `test-dummy_hash.R` overwhelmingly assert shape (`dim()`), type (`is.numeric()`), or dense==sparse *identity* — never a hand-computed expected numeric value for the interesting cases (sublinear TF-IDF, double normalization, LDA topic sums, the person/preposition counters, `num_terms`/`sequence_length` boundary values).

This is the systemic root cause behind several real bugs found in a recent audit (see #314, #315, #316, #317, #325) — each one passed the existing test suite because the tests never checked a single computed number against a hand-worked expected value.

## Suggested change

For each numeric weighting/counting function, add at least one test asserting a specific expected value computed by hand or against a reference (`stats::`, a second implementation, or manual arithmetic), not just shape.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **B1**.

title: add `is_tokenlist()` helper
Use recipes_map_cols() in bake() methods that transform columns in place
description:
recipes is gaining an exported `recipes_map_cols()` helper (tidymodels/recipes#1543, tidymodels/recipes#1556, tidymodels/recipes#1558) for use in `bake()` methods of steps that transform columns in place. Assigning one column at a time in a `for` loop (`new_data[[col_name]] <- ...`) copies the whole data frame on each iteration, which is quadratic in the number of columns. `recipes_map_cols()` computes all the new columns first and assigns them in bulk. In recipes, baking 8,000 factor columns through `step_other()` dropped from 5.14s to 1.26s.

The following `bake()` methods in textrecipes use the slow pattern and could be converted:

- `step_clean_levels()` (`R/clean_levels.R:135`)
- `step_untokenize()` (`R/untokenize.R:125`)
- `step_tokenize()` (`R/tokenize.R:349`)
- `step_pos_filter()` (`R/pos_filter.R:124`)
- `step_tokenize_bpe()` (`R/tokenize_bpe.R:195`)
- `step_tokenize_wordpiece()` (`R/tokenize_wordpiece.R:145`)
- `step_ngram()` (`R/ngram.R:157`)
- `step_stem()` (`R/stem.R:155`)
- `step_text_normalization()` (`R/text_normalization.R:146`)
- `step_lemma()` (`R/lemma.R:116`)
- `step_tokenfilter()` (`R/tokenfilter.R:220`)
- `step_stopwords()` (`R/stopwords.R:184`)
- `step_tokenize_sentencepiece()` (`R/tokenize_sentencepiece.R:197`)

Note that `step_untokenize()` and `step_text_normalization()` each assign twice per column, so they benefit doubly.

This is blocked on the recipes release that exports `recipes_map_cols()`.

title: bake.step_tokenize() silently recycles undersized tokenizer output
description:
## Problem

`tokenizer_fun` (R/tokenize.R:350-354, shared by `step_tokenize`, `step_tokenize_bpe`, `step_tokenize_sentencepiece`, `step_tokenize_wordpiece`) does:

```r
new_data[[col_name]] <- tokenizer_fun(...)
```

with no length check. If a custom tokenizer (or plausibly an external engine under some input) returns a list shorter than `nrow(new_data)`, R's silent recycling duplicates rows' tokens rather than erroring.

## Repro

A `custom_token` returning a length-1 list for 3 input rows produces 3 identical output rows with no warning.

## Suggested fix

Assert `length(out) == length(x)` (or a vctrs size-check) in `tokenizer_fun`, with a clear `cli_abort` naming the offending column/engine.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **A5**.

title: step_clean_levels() silently fails to clean character columns consistently
description:
## Problem

`check_type()` allows `"string"` columns in `step_clean_levels`, but `prep.step_clean_levels()` (R/clean_levels.R:126-147) computes `orig <- purrr::map(training[, col_names], levels)` — `levels()` on a character vector is always `NULL`, so the trained cleaning map for character columns is always empty. At `bake()` this forces a fallback that calls `janitor::make_clean_names()` directly on the *values* every bake call, which is designed to dedupe column names, not row values — so identical input values get different output depending on row position within the batch being baked.

## Repro

```r
dat <- tibble::tibble(name = c("Foo Bar", "Foo Bar", "Baz Qux"))
recipe(~., data = dat) |> step_clean_levels(name) |>
  prep(strings_as_factors = FALSE) |> bake(new_data = NULL)
#   name
#   foo_bar
#   foo_bar_2   <- same input value as row 1, cleaned differently!
#   baz_qux
```

This also means the documented "novel levels become NA" behavior never triggers for character columns, and `tidy()` reports an empty mapping even though bake did transform values. Reachable through the now-recommended `recipe(..., strings_as_factors = FALSE)` path.

## Suggested fix

In `prep.step_clean_levels()`, build the cleaning dictionary from `unique(training[[col_name]])` (coerced to character) rather than `levels()`, and apply that trained dictionary consistently at bake (novel → NA), instead of re-deriving `make_clean_names` per bake call.

---

title: src/ngram.c mislabels non-UTF-8 input as UTF-8
description:
## Problem

`fill_one_ngram()` in src/ngram.c (lines 26, 29, 38, 42, 48) reads raw bytes with `CHAR(STRING_ELT(x, i))` and always tags the output with `Rf_mkCharCE(out_elt, CE_UTF8)`, without ever calling `Rf_translateCharUTF8()`. For latin1/native-encoded input (common on Windows or with legacy-encoded text), the raw bytes are not valid UTF-8, so the mislabeled string throws real errors in ordinary downstream operations (`nchar()`, `toupper()`), not just a display glitch.

## Repro

A latin1 "café" byte sequence ngrammed with `n = 1` round-trips as a string reporting `Encoding() == "UTF-8"` whose bytes are invalid UTF-8; `nchar()`/`toupper()` on the result throw `invalid multibyte string`/`invalid input ... in 'utf8towcs'`.

## Suggested fix

Use `Rf_translateCharUTF8()` when reading the input bytes (in both the size-computation pass and the fill pass), then continue tagging output `CE_UTF8` (translation guarantees valid UTF-8).

---

title: count_functions.R has several doc/implementation mismatches beyond the person/preposition bug
description:
## Problem

In R/count_functions.R:

- `n_uq_urls` (:78-81): regex `"https?"` only ever captures the literal substring `"http"`/`"https"`, so `n_distinct` is capped at 2 regardless of how many distinct URLs exist — "number of unique urls" is not meaningfully computed.
- `n_charS`/`n_uq_charS` (:10-22): docs claim urls/hashtags/mentions are excluded, but the code only strips whitespace.
- `n_extraspaces` (:62-64): docs say "more than 1 consecutive space," but the regex `"\\s{2}|\\t|\\n"` also fires on a single tab/newline.
- NA handling is inconsistent across the list: most `n_*` functions propagate `NA`, the `n_uq_*` unique-count functions return `1` for `NA` input, and the person/preposition functions return `0` — undocumented and untested.

## Suggested change

Align each function's regex/logic with its documented behavior; document the NA convention once, consistently, or make all functions handle NA the same way.

title: step_tf()/step_tfidf() docs describe the wrong denominator for term frequency / norm = 'l1'
description:
## Problem

R/tf.R's roxygen `@details` says "divide the count by the total number of words in the document"; R/tfidf.R's `@param norm` doc says "scale by the number of words in the document". The actual denominator (`rowSums()`) is computed on the dtm produced by `tokenlist_to_dtm()`, which only counts tokens that match the *trained vocabulary* — any token dropped by a custom `vocabulary` argument, or (very commonly, since the docs "strongly advise" it) an upstream `step_tokenfilter()`, is excluded from both numerator and denominator. So the real formula is "count / count-of-in-vocabulary-tokens," not "count / total-words," whenever the vocabulary is restricted.

## Repro

With a restricted vocabulary, `tf` values reflect `count / in-vocab-count` (e.g. 2/5, 3/5 for a document with 9 total words but only 5 in-vocabulary tokens), not `count / 9`.

## Suggested fix

Reword docs to "divide by the total number of (in-vocabulary) tokens in the document" in both files.

---

title: step_texthash()/step_dummy_hash() crash R when num_terms = 0
description:
## Problem

`check_number_whole(x$num_terms, min = 0, arg = "num_terms")` in `prep.step_texthash` (R/texthash.R:170) and `prep.step_dummy_hash` (R/dummy_hash.R:181) both accept `0`. At bake time this reaches `text2vec::create_dtm()` / `hash_vectorizer(hash_size = 0)`, which segfaults the R process (not a catchable R error — it aborts the whole session).

## Repro

```r
library(recipes)
library(textrecipes)

recipe(~text, data = tibble::tibble(text = "a b c")) |>
  step_tokenize(text) |>
  step_texthash(text, num_terms = 0) |>
  prep()
#  *** caught segfault ***
#  address 0x10f591c6c, cause 'invalid permissions'
#  ... An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
```

The same crash reproduces for `step_dummy_hash()`.

Existing "bad args" tests only check `num_terms = -4`, never `0`.

## Suggested fix

Change `min = 0` to `min = 1` in both `prep.step_texthash` and `prep.step_dummy_hash`. Add regression tests for `num_terms = 0` asserting a clean `cli_abort`, not a crash.

title: step_clean_levels() backwards-compatibility shim is dead code, can silently no-op cleaning
description:
## Problem

The "Backwards compatibility with 1.0.3 (#230)" fix-up in R/clean_levels.R:130-135 captures `col_names <- names(object$clean)` *before* fixing up the names, then the loop below reuses that stale (still-`NULL`) `col_names`. When `object$clean` genuinely has no outer names (the exact legacy scenario this code claims to handle), the loop runs zero times and `bake()` silently returns data completely uncleaned.

## Repro

Stripping `names(object$clean)` on a trained object and baking returns the input completely unchanged, with no error/warning.

## Suggested fix

Compute `col_names` from `object$clean` *after* the backwards-compat name assignment, or (better) store column names in a dedicated `columns` field instead of deriving them from `names(clean)`.

---

title: step_lda() bake() is non-deterministic and often degenerate
description:
## Problem

`word_dims_newtext()` (R/lda.R:269-283), called from `bake.step_lda` (R/lda.R:195), calls `lda_model$fit_transform(dtm, n_iter = n_iter)` instead of `lda_model$transform(dtm, n_iter = n_iter)`. `fit_transform` re-fits topic assignments from whatever documents are in the current batch; `transform` is the text2vec method meant to project new documents onto the already-fitted model. Compounding this, the vocabulary at bake time is rebuilt from scratch from `new_data`'s own tokens with different (stricter) pruning than the vocabulary used at `prep()`, so bake never reuses the trained vocabulary/dtm at all.

## Repro (against `modeldata::tate_text`)

- Baking the *training* data itself: topic-column row sums range 0-1 (mean 0.847), not the ~1 an LDA distribution must sum to.
- Baking a small 5-row batch: all topic columns are exactly 0, with a console warning `dtm has 0 rows. Empty iterator?` that's silently swallowed.
- Baking row 1 alone gives `(0,0,0,0,0)`; baking the *same* row as part of a 100-row batch gives `(0.4,0,0.3,0.3,0)` — the output for a fixed document changes depending on what else is in the same `bake()` call, violating the basic recipes contract that `bake()` is a deterministic, row-independent transform of the fitted step.

## Suggested fix

Call `lda_model$transform(dtm, n_iter = n_iter)` in `word_dims_newtext`, and build the new-data dtm against the vocabulary/dictionary learned during `prep()` rather than re-deriving it from `new_data` alone.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **A2**.

title: options argument crashes bake() for spacyr/tokenizers.bpe/sentencepiece engines
description:
## Problem

`tokenizer_fun()` does `rlang::call_modify(token_expr, !!!options)` then evaluates. The bake-time closures for `engine = "spacyr"` and `"tokenizers.bpe"` (R/tokenizer-spacyr.R, R/tokenizer-tokenizersbpe.R), and `R/tokenizer-sentencepiece.R`, take only `x` with no `...`, so any non-empty `options` (or re-used training-time `options`) throws `unused argument` at bake, called from R/tokenize.R:388-408, R/tokenize_bpe.R:196-200, R/tokenize_sentencepiece.R:198-203.

The `udpipe` and `wordpiece` closures correctly accept `...` and don't have this problem — an inconsistency across the engine family.

## Evidence

Confirmed via the general mechanism (`f <- function(x) ...; call_modify` + non-empty list throws `unused argument`) and static trace to each call site; no test in the suite sets non-empty `options` for these engines, which is why it's unguarded.

## Suggested fix

Add `...` to the spacyr/tokenizers.bpe/sentencepiece closures, or stop re-passing training-only `options` at bake time and document which of `options`/`training_options` apply at which stage.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **A6**.

title: tokenmerge.R reads object$column (singular) instead of object$columns (plural)
description:
## Problem

R/tokenmerge.R:126 reads `object$column` (singular) where the step object only ever has `object$columns` (plural). This currently works only because `$` partial-matches on lists — it reads as a typo and is fragile against future field additions (a new field starting with "column" would silently break it).

## Suggested change

Change `object$column` to `object$columns` at R/tokenmerge.R:126.

title: step_stem() silently drops lemma/pos tokenlist attributes
description:
## Problem

`tokenlist_apply()` (R/tokenlist.R:219-232, used by `bake.step_stem`) reconstructs the result with only `tokens`, never forwarding `lemma`/`pos` the way `tokenlist_filter()` does. A user who tokenizes with POS/lemma tagging (spacyr/udpipe) and then stems loses those attributes with no warning.

## Repro

`step_stem(text) |> step_pos_filter(text)` after a POS-tagging tokenizer throws `'text' doesn't have a pos attribute. i Make sure the tokenization step includes part of speech tagging.` — even though tokenization did include POS tagging; the error misleadingly points at the wrong step.

## Suggested fix

Have `tokenlist_apply` propagate `lemma`/`pos` unchanged (stemming doesn't change token count/alignment), mirroring `tokenlist_filter_function`; or explicitly document the attribute loss and improve the `pos_filter`/`lemma` error messages to mention it as a possible cause.

title: 7 of 26 default step_textfeature() count functions always return ~0 for real text
description:
## Problem

`first_person`, `first_personp`, `second_person`, `second_personp`, `third_person`, `to_be`, and `prepositions` in R/count_functions.R:93-188 each do:

```r
purrr::map_int(x, \(.x) sum(fp %in% .x, na.rm = TRUE))
```

where `x` is the raw, untokenized character column (`step_textfeature` operates on whole-string character columns — confirmed via `check_type(training[, col_names], types = c("string","factor","ordered"))` in R/textfeature.R:140), and `.x` is therefore one whole document string. `fp %in% .x` tests whole-value set membership — "is the word `is` literally equal to the entire document string" — not "does the document contain the word `is`."

## Repro

```r
devtools::load_all()
to_be(c("This is a test string", "we are the champions"))
#> [1] 0 0        # both clearly contain "is"/"are"
first_person(c("I would not eat them here or there.", "I would not eat them anywhere."))
#> [1] 0 0        # both clearly contain "I"
```

These 7 functions make up 27% of the default `count_functions` feature set and silently return near-constant-0 columns for essentially all real input. Existing tests only check shape/type, never a computed value, which is why this was unguarded.

## Suggested fix

Tokenize `.x` (e.g. `stringi::stri_extract_all_words(.x)`) before testing membership, rather than testing the raw string against the word list.

---
Filed from an audit of the package; see internal report ID **A3**.

title: show_tokens()'s argument validation silently ignores its upper bound
description:
## Problem

R/show_tokens.R:29 does:

```r
check_number_whole(n, min = 0, nrow(rec$template))
```

`check_number_whole`'s signature places `max` after `...`, so the bound lands in `...` and is never applied. Worse, whenever validation needs to actually fail, the stray `...` argument corrupts the error-reporting call and produces a nonsensical error (`Error: 'class' must be a character vector, not the number 2.`) instead of a useful message.

## Evidence

Reproduced directly; there is no test file at all for `show_tokens()` (`tests/testthat/test-show_tokens.R` doesn't exist), which is why this shipped unnoticed.

## Suggested fix

`check_number_whole(n, min = 0, max = nrow(rec$template))`. Add a `test-show_tokens.R`.

---

title: step_ngram()/step_sequence_onehot() accept invalid 0 arguments, surfacing confusing downstream errors
description:
## Problem

R/ngram.R:133-134 and R/sequence_onehot.R:147 both use `check_number_whole(x, min = 0, ...)` even though the documented minimum is 1 (`num_tokens`, `min_num_tokens`, `sequence_length`).

For ngram, this pushes the failure into a deep, unrelated C-level error (`n must be a positive integer`), and there's no check anywhere that `min_num_tokens <= num_tokens` (only enforced in C, whose own message has a typo: "n_min must be less then n.").

For `sequence_length = 0`, the failure surfaces as an unrelated `dimnames` length-mismatch error caused by `paste()`'s zero-length-argument quirk, not a clear "must be ≥ 1" message.

## Evidence

Both reproduced directly with concrete error text.

## Suggested fix

Change `min = 0` to `min = 1` in both; add an explicit `min_num_tokens <= num_tokens` check in `prep.step_ngram` so the on-topic error surfaces instead of the C-level fallback.

---

title: TF-IDF produces negative values when sublinear_tf = TRUE
description:
## Problem

In `dtm_to_tfidf` (R/tfidf.R), the block does:

```r
dtm <- normalize(dtm, norm)
if (sublinear_tf) { dtm@x <- 1 + log(dtm@x) }
```

L1/L2 normalization is applied to the raw counts *before* the sublinear (`1 + log(tf)`) transform, so by the time the log is taken, `dtm@x` holds fractions (count/rowSum) rather than raw counts. `log()` of a value < 1 is negative, so `1 + log(fraction)` can be negative — and multiplying by a non-negative idf then yields a negative TF-IDF score, which should be mathematically impossible for standard sublinear TF-IDF.

## Repro

```r
d <- tibble::tibble(text = c("a a a a a a a b", "a b b b b b b b"))
recipe(~text, data = d) |> step_tokenize(text) |>
  step_tfidf(text, sublinear_tf = TRUE, norm = "l1") |> prep() |> bake(NULL)
#   tfidf_text_a tfidf_text_b
# 1        0.601       -0.748
# 2       -0.748        0.601
```

Applying sublinear scaling to raw counts first (as the docs describe: "replace the term frequency with 1 + log(TF)") gives non-negative values, e.g. doc 1's `a`: `(1+log(7)) * idf ≈ 2.04`.

## Suggested fix

Apply the sublinear transform to the raw counts *before* calling `normalize()` (swap the two blocks, or normalize a separate copy). Existing tests for `sublinear_tf` only check dense==sparse identity, never a hand-computed expected value, which is why this shipped unnoticed.

title: tf_weight()'s double normalization scheme produces NaN for zero-token documents
description:
## Problem

R/tf.R:318-321: unlike the "term frequency" branch two lines above (which explicitly zeroes rows where `rowSums == 0`), the "double normalization" scheme has no guard for `max_ftd == 0`, so an empty document yields `0/0 = NaN` silently.

## Repro

A two-document batch where one document is empty (`""`) produces `NaN` in every weight column for that row.

## Suggested fix

Add the same `res[rowsums_x == 0, ] <- weight` (or `0`) guard used in the "term frequency" branch.

---

title: Generate a sparse tf-idf matrix from a tokenlist in a recipe step
description:
Hello,
I am currently trying to use textrecipes in a project as part of our NLP pipeline in connection with {tidymodels}. At one point I came across a problem for which I have not yet found a solution. My problem is that the step `textrecipes::step_tfidf` apparently only generates a dense matrix (in the form of a tibble) and not a sparse matrix (dgCMatrix) and this leads to such a large object that I cannot process it in memory. The details in the documentation for this function also describe that `step_tokenfilter` should be executed in advance for this purpose. I would be very reluctant to do this, however, as I assume that in a sparse format - which I use as a blueprint in the modelling workflow anyway - the resulting object is sufficiently small. Meanwhile, tidymodels also seems to be able to cope with sparse matrices as input. 
So my question is, is there a way to convert from a tokenlist representation to a sparse tf-idf (or other dtm) representation in a recipe step or to use another low-memory format as an intermediate step (such as the format from {tidytext}).
It would also be interesting to know whether this is currently only a technical restriction or whether the idea behind it is that there is no legitimate modelling assumption in which we cannot (better) manage with a token filter or another word embedding?

Many thanks in advance and best regards!

title: Token filtering step based on relative frequency (length of source document)
description:
Hello,
First of all, thank you very much for developing this package! 

I was wondering if it was possible in the token filtering step (`step_tokenfilter()`) to implement a method based on the relative and not absolute frequency of a token's appearance. For example, here's my code:

```
data_train <- tibble(sentence = c("This is words", "They are nice !", "Pretty pretty pretty good !", "Another sentence that is in doc2"),
                                   doc = c("doc1", "doc2", "doc2", "doc2"))

data_rec <- recipe(x ~ sentence, data = data_train) %>%
      step_tokenize(sentence) %>%
      step_stopwords(sentence, custom_stopword_source = stopwords_list) %>%
      step_tokenfilter(sentence, max_tokens = 1000) %>%
      step_tfidf(sentence)


```

Indeed, the absolute frequency-based filter is largely influenced by the potential length of the document in which the sentences are found. The longer the text, the more likely the token will appear. It would be interesting to be able to filter tokens based on relative frequency (based on the total number of words in each value of the `doc` variable in the example) before calculating the tf-idf on these extracted tokens, wouldn't it?

Thx in advance ;)

title: step_negation function?
description:
I have seen articles suggesting that creating unique tokens for negated words can improve results (e.g. https://analyticsindiamag.com/when-to-use-negation-handling-in-sentiment-analysis/). Would this make sense for a step function?

I do it crudely now by using these approaches

```
library(tidymodels)
library(textrecipes)
library(tidytext)
library(stringr)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'stringr'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:recipes':
#> 
#>     fixed

tate_text <- tate_text |>
  select(medium, year)

tate_nots = tibble(medium = "Etching on not canvas", year = 2000)
tate_text = bind_rows(tate_nots,tate_text)

# APPROACH 1: preproccess raw data
tate_text |> 
  mutate(medium = str_replace(medium, "not ","not_"))
#> # A tibble: 4,285 × 2
#>    medium                                                   year
#>    <chr>                                                   <dbl>
#>  1 Etching on not_canvas                                    2000
#>  2 Video, monitor or projection, colour and sound (stereo)  1990
#>  3 Etching on paper                                         1990
#>  4 Etching on paper                                         1990
#>  5 Etching on paper                                         1990
#>  6 Oil paint on canvas                                      1990
#>  7 Oil paint on canvas                                      1990
#>  8 Acrylic paint on paper                                   1990
#>  9 Woodcut on paper                                         1990
#> 10 Oil paint and wax on canvas                              1990
#> # ℹ 4,275 more rows

# APPROACH 2: process tokenized data
detect_negations <- function(tokens,negation_words = c("not")) {
  # function to negate tokenized data
  tokens <- tokens %>% rowid_to_column(var="word_num")
```

title: Model (glmnet, classification) class prediction of an item differs when item is a single item in a tibble
description:
I observed a strange thing when collecting predictions from a glmnet classification model. When a item is part of a large dataset it gets a different class prediction than when it is a single item in a tibble.

See script below (from https://juliasilge.com/blog/nber-papers/)
```r
#### Start Script
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(textrecipes)

GetData <- FALSE

if (GetData) {
  papers <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-09-28/papers.csv")
  programs <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-09-28/programs.csv")
  paper_authors <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-09-28/paper_authors.csv")
  paper_programs <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2021/2021-09-28/paper_programs.csv")
  
  
  papers_joined <-
    paper_programs %>%
    left_join(programs) %>%
    left_join(papers) %>%
    filter(!is.na(program_category)) %>%
    distinct(paper, program_category, year, title)

  saveRDS(papers_joined,'papers.rds')  
} else {
  papers_joined <- readRDS('papers.rds')
}


set.seed(123)
nber_split <- initial_split(papers_joined, strata = program_category)
nber_train <- training(nber_split)
nber_test <- testing(nber_split)

nber_rec <-
  recipe(program_category ~ year + title, data = nber_train) %>%
  step_tokenize(title) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(title, max_tokens = 200) %>%
  step_tfidf(title)

multi_spec <-
  multinom_reg(penalty = 0.00428, mixture = 1) %>%
  set_mode("classification") %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

nber_wf   <- workflow(nber_rec, multi_spec)
nber_fit  <- nber_wf %>% fit(data=nber_train)
```

title: Is tokenlist the right word?
description:

title: Support all_tokenized_predictors(), similar to e.g. all_numeric_predictors()
description:
## Feature

The recipes package provides `all_numeric_predictors()` and `all_nominal_predictors()` for applying a recipe to every variable of a particular role and type. It would be great if textrecipes supported something analogous like `all_tokenized_predictors()`.

For example, suppose I wanted to apply the recipe in the README to 9 essays, not just 2:

```
library(recipes)
library(textrecipes)
library(modeldata)

data(okc_text)

# In this case could use `starts_with("essay")`, but general point
# is that I might want to add/remove some variables from the recipe
okc_rec <- recipe(~  ., data = okc_text) %>%
  step_tokenize(essay0, essay1, essay2, essay3, essay4, essay5,
                essay6, essay7, essay8, essay9) %>%
  step_stopwords(has_type("other")) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(has_type("other"), max_tokens = 10) %>%
  step_tfidf(has_type("other"))

okc_rec %>%
  prep() %>%
  juice()
```

Right now, my workaround is `has_type("other")`, as above. This works as long as the only "other" columns are `textrecipes_tokenlist` (especially as tidymodels expands what they use list columns for), and in any case it's harder to understand the intent. (I don't have the understanding of `has_type()` to know if this requires changes to the recipes package as well).

This is especially useful when I'm rapidly changing which columns I decide to include and tokenize (right now, I have to edit every step of the process; not only tokenizing but also stopwords, tokenfilter, stemming and tf/tfidf, and it's easy for them to get out of sync). I find I'm operations like tf in particular are always done on all tokenized predictors.

description:
Hello 👋 

In the most recent [CRAN release](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/recipes/index.html) of {recipes}, we took the first step towards [updating the printing infrastructure to use {cli}](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/426). See example below:

```r
# Old
print.step_pls <- function(x, width = max(20, options()$width - 35), ...) {
  cat("PLS feature extraction with ")
  printer(x$columns, x$terms, x$trained, width = width)
  invisible(x)
}

# New
print.step_pls <- function(x, width = max(20, options()$width - 35), ...) {
  title <- "PLS feature extraction with "
  print_step(x$columns, x$terms, x$trained, width = width, title = title)
  invisible(x)
}
```

title: Analog to TfIdfVectorizer
description:
@EmilHvitfeldt thanks for starting this; got here from https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/192.

I've been meaning to write a `step_tfidf` that does something roughly equivalent to [`sklearn`s `TfIdfVectorizer`](http://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer.html), though hopefully without quite so many arguments. This package's existence seems like a good excuse to finally do that.

So my questions then are:
1. are you open to a PR for this, or do you already have something in the works?
1. all-in-one, or layered? All-in-one would mean the input to this step is one row per document (e.g. a `doc` columns with long-form text in it), and layered meaning this would need to be called _after_ `step_tokenize`. I think I lean towards the layered approach, because otherwise there'd be a ton of duplication between the two, but all-in-one might be more user-friendly? One argument _against_ the layers is that the output of `step_tokenizer` will only ever be an intermediate one (can't model from the output, right?), so perhaps it should be a functional input to other steps, rather than it's own step?
1. Should filtering (like with the `max_df`/`min_df` args in sklearn) be done in this step, or in a subsequent step? Something seems lovely and idiomatic about the layered approach, but filtering on document frequency after-the-fact would be way less efficient.

title: Word embeddings
description:
I want to include word embedding steps in this package at some point.

Asked in https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/issues/9 I'm going to answer here in the main issue.

I would like to have a step for each word embedding we implement. I want this approach because I fear that a general `step_embed` would end up with a lot of arguments as each embedding might need different arguments.

As of right now the https://github.com/dselivanov/text2vec package is already imported and it allows for both text2vec and Glove so it would be a nice place to start. Later we can look at other embeddings such as fasttext which would require additional dependencies.

We would like to have some default pre-trained embeddings (for sure), but in the future it would also be nice for some custom trained embeddings to be used. Some investigation on the correct format would have to be done.
The priority right now is to have the embeddings working, and then we can implement user-supplied embeddings after.

title: Pre-tokenization steps
description:
The step_tokenize help says "Working will 'textrecipes' will always start by calling 'step_tokenize' followed by modifying and filtering steps." There are some things that are helpful to implement *before* tokenization, to avoid losing meaning. Examples in my current demo:

* spelling (I ended up just doing this in the original google sheet for the moment to make my life easier, but it could be implemented with hunspell)
* textclean::replace_contraction
* textclean::replace_time
* textclean::replace_number

For the demo, I rolled them up into a custom tokenizer, but it seems like they could fit here to provide users with some tasks that are likely to be common during text modeling.

Any thoughts?

Sorry for all the issue, hopefully I can help close some once I'm done sorting through this demo!

title: Upcoming changes for tune
description:
(also pinging @jonthegeek since this would probably affect him too)

There are a few changes for recipes-related packages for the upcoming `tune` package. 

First, for `tune` to know what is _possible to optimize_, there is an S3 method in `tune` called `tunable`. It basically returns a tibble with a row for every parameter that someone would want to modify. The ones related to `textrecipes` are already in `tune` (from [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/c964b8d1c0c490ef7c40bc4400c84a7fe257be16/R/tunable.R#L161) to [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/c964b8d1c0c490ef7c40bc4400c84a7fe257be16/R/tunable.R#L219)). Please edit as you see fit in case I under- or -overestimated what people would want. 

But here's the hitch: in r-devel (aka R 4.0), there is a big change in how R looks up S3 methods. In our case, there is a generic defined in `tune` but method s in other packages. In this case, the package with the methods has to register those methods when the package starts up. Our boilerplate `.onLoad ()` code to do that for all relavant steps is in the devel version of recipes [here](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/cff3d454823be3a1f7f2924bce6946f6d186da9b/R/0_imports.R#L37). The `s3_register()` function is form `vctrs` but we've decided that, for now , we should just copy it to the package that needs. it.  

This _should_ solve the issue but I haven't been able to properly test it on 4.0 since this change causes a bunch of other parts to fail. It passes my tests with versions < 4.0. We have used this with plenty of other packages but I can't tell if it is _enough_ to solve the issue. 

As a side-effect, we would probably want any tunable parameter to be associated with a corresponding parameter object from `dials`. You could add this in your package is you want (like I did for [`discrim`](https://github.com/tidymodels/discrim/blob/master/R/parameters.R)) or do a PR into `dials`. I've added some for these steps in the current version of `dials` but maybe I missed some. 

Let me know if you have any questions or concerns about this.

title: step_stem(..., options='russian') seems doesn't work
description:
reprex() has some problems with Russian locale so I edit something manually

``` r
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, tidymodels, textrecipes)

data <- tibble(y = 0, text = "коты")  # "cats" in Russian. 

# this doesn't work, ignoring 'language' argument
recipe(y ~ ., data = data) %>% 
    step_tokenize(text) %>% 
    step_stem(text, options = list(language = "russian")) %>% 
    prep(data) %>% 
    juice() %>% 
    pull(text)
#> [[1]]
#> "коты"

# only this way works
recipe(y ~ ., data = data) %>% 
    step_tokenize(text) %>% 
    step_stem(text, custom_stemmer = partial(SnowballC::wordStem, language = "russian")) %>% 
    prep(data) %>% 
    juice() %>% 
    pull(text)
#> [[1]]
#> "кот"
```

I did `debug(Snowball::wordStem) and couldn't find Russian language in options. Porter stemmer only.

title: Error in UseMethod(\"prep\"): no applicable method for 'prep' applied to an object of class 'step_tokenize'
description:
### Brief description of the problem

I have encountered an error trying to follow Julia Silge's Tidy Tuesday blogpost on [sentiment analysis in Animal Crossing reviews](https://juliasilge.com/blog/animal-crossing/). 

This may be related to running the code on Windows 10. Or at least the code obviously runs well for Julia. It also runs perfectly for me in a [docker container](https://hub.docker.com/r/rocker/tidyverse) running R 4.0 on Debian (with tidymodels, textrecipes and glmnet etc installed from source).

I get a warning that `All models failed in tune_grid(). See the .notes column` when I try to tune a grid as below and then `error: all of the models failed` when I run collect_metrics. The warning reads: `recipe: Error in UseMethod(\"prep\"): no applicable method for 'prep' applied to an object of class \"c('step_tokenize', 'step')\"`.

All packages are up to date off Cran and I am running R 4.0.

I've created a MWE below by applying Julia's code to the "The War of the Worlds" and "Pride and Prejudice" loaded from Project Gutenberg as per [here](https://www.hvitfeldt.me/blog/text-classification-with-tidymodels/), but subsetting to use the first thousand rows from each.

When I was working on tidymodels/tune#315, I noticed that there are `tunable` methods for recipe _steps_ from textrecipes in tune. The `tunable` methods for most recipe steps are in recipes itself ([for example](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/a1d3aa499b7649b7324da4d5bff971a80bf56c42/R/pca.R#L316)) but it has been tricky to register the methods and get it all to work.

The new version of generics that just went to CRAN now includes `tunable` (along with `required_pkgs`) so this should be much simpler now.

I can put together a PR if you don't get to it before me!
